rawFindings.title: State BEING_CAPTURED set after start rather than before
rawFindings.explanation: The state BEING_CAPTURED is set after calling self._start() in the start() function, whereas the previous code set this state before. If _start() depends on the state being BEING_CAPTURED, this reordering may cause race conditions or logic errors in asynchronous code responding to the state.
rawFindings.suggestion: Move 'self.state = BEING_CAPTURED;' line before the call to self._start(capturingUrl + '?id=' + self.id).
rawFindings.failureAfterChange: Input: Calling start(url) followed immediately by an event handler triggered by _start() which checks self.state to be BEING_CAPTURED. Result: Handler does not detect correct state because state is not yet set, causing erroneous behavior.
